name: SSH Hijacking
description:
Adversaries may hijack a legitimate user's SSH session to move laterally within an environment. Secure Shell (SSH) is a standard means of remote access on Linux and macOS systems. It allows a user to connect to another system via an encrypted tunnel, commonly authenticating through a password, certificate or the use of an asymmetric encryption key pair.

In order to move laterally from a compromised host, adversaries may take advantage of trust relationships established with other systems via public key authentication in active SSH sessions by hijacking an existing connection to another system. This may occur through compromising the SSH agent itself or by having access to the agent's socket. If an adversary is able to obtain root access, then hijacking SSH sessions is likely trivial.(Citation: Slideshare Abusing SSH)(Citation: SSHjack Blackhat)(Citation: Clockwork SSH Agent Hijacking)(Citation: Breach Post-mortem SSH Hijack)

[SSH Hijacking](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1563/001) differs from use of [SSH](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/004) because it hijacks an existing SSH session rather than creating a new session using [Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078).

telemetry.name: Logon Session Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a logon session with account and logon-type context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit Logon and collect successful session creation on the receiving host; join session/logon IDs rather than only account names.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: Network Connection Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of an endpoint network connection linked to a process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable scoped Sysmon NetworkConnect (3), disabled by default, or a platform-equivalent process-aware network sensor.

For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

telemetry.name: Process Metadata
telemetry.description: Point-in-time process properties such as owner, executable and start time.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect read-only process inventory with PID plus start time/stable identity, command line and collection time; restrict access to potentially sensitive arguments.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for SSH Session Hijacking

analytics.name: Analytic 0710
analytics.guidance: Suspicious reuse of SSH agent sockets across multiple users or processes, anomalous access to ~/.ssh/ or /tmp/ssh-* sockets, and abnormal patterns of lateral movement via SSH without new authentication events. Defender view: detect when one process accesses another user's SSH agent or when an existing SSH connection is used to pivot unexpectedly.

tuning.description: Tune alerts for cross-user access to SSH agent sockets.
Correlate lack of authentication with lateral SSH activity within a short timeframe.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: open or connect syscalls on /tmp/ssh-* or $SSH_AUTH_SOCK

log_sources.name: auditd:EXECVE
log_sources.channel: Execution of ssh/scp/sftp without corresponding authentication log

log_sources.name: NSM:Connections
log_sources.channel: Missing new login event but session activity continues

analytics.name: Analytic 0711
analytics.guidance: Unusual access to SSH agent sockets in /tmp/ or /private/tmp, process access to another user’s $SSH_AUTH_SOCK, and lateral SSH activity without corresponding login events. Defender view: correlation of socket access with anomalous network flows to internal systems.

tuning.description: Limit detection to monitored SSH agent socket directories.
Establish normal SSH agent ownership and expected usage for tuning.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Process opening SSH_AUTH_SOCK or /tmp/ssh-* socket not owned by same UID

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Execution of ssh or sftp without corresponding login event

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Session reuse without new auth event

software.name: MEDUSA
software.description: [MEDUSA](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1220) can be configured to capture SSH credentials via SSH hijacking.(Citation: Google Cloud Mandiant UNC3886 2024)

references.description: Punsaen Boonyakarn, Shawn Chew, Logeswaran Nadarajan, Mathew Potaczek, Jakub Jozwiak, and Alex Marvi. (2024, June 18). Cloaked and Covert: Uncovering UNC3886 Espionage Operations. Retrieved September 24, 2024.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.description: Ensure proper file permissions are set and harden system to prevent root privilege escalation opportunities.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Do not allow remote access via SSH as root or other privileged accounts.

mitigations.name: Password Policies
mitigations.description: Ensure SSH key pairs have strong passwords and refrain from using key-store technologies such as ssh-agent unless they are properly protected.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Ensure that agent forwarding is disabled on systems that do not explicitly require this feature to prevent misuse. (Citation: Symantec SSH and ssh-agent)

references.description: Hatch, B. (2004, November 22). SSH and ssh-agent. Retrieved January 8, 2018.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.
